title: Informal Conjecture on reflexive graphs and coloring abundance
statement_text: Graphs with a large number of colorings tend to be reflexive.
context_text: Colorings are considered here for $k=3$. A 3-coloring of a graph $X$ is viewed as a partition of $V(X)$ into 3 independent sets, its color classes. The 3-coloring complex $B(X)$ is the graph whose vertices are all color classes occurring in some 3-coloring of $X$, two classes being adjacent if they appear together in a 3-coloring; under mild conditions (e.g. $X$ contains an edge) $B(X)$ is again 3-colorable, and each 3-coloring of $X$ gives a triangle of $B(X)$. Fisk showed that, when every edge of $X$ lies in a triangle and $X$ has no isolated vertices, the canonical map $\phi_X$ sending a vertex $v$ to the set of color classes containing $v$ is a homomorphism from $X$ to $B^2(X)=B(B(X))$; $X$ is reflexive if $\phi_X$ is an isomorphism. The paper studies 3-edge-colorings of cubic graphs in which half-edges (edges with only one end) are allowed: a cubic graph $G$ is edge-reflexive if its line graph $L(G)$ is reflexive. The main result is that a connected cubic outerplanar graph (with half-edges) is edge-reflexive if and only if it is triangle-free; $K_{3,3}$, even prisms and many theta graphs are also edge-reflexive. There is no obvious reason why any graph should be reflexive, and the authors state that the real open question is why there are so many reflexive graphs. The informal claim that graphs with many colorings tend to be reflexive is supported by their results and extensive computations, although it seems counterintuitive: many colorings make the complex $B(X)$ large, so it may have too many colorings for $X$ to be reflexive. It is not given a precise mathematical formulation.
notes: Stated in prose in the introduction without a labelled environment; backed by 'extensive computational evidence' but not given a precise mathematical formulation. The paper text is truncated mid-proof, so further conjectures in later sections may be missing.
paper_title: Reflexive coloring complexes for 3-edge-colorings of cubic graphs
